memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "On the eighth day they must bring two male lambs and one ewe lamb a year old, each without defect, along with three-tenths of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with olive oil for a grain offering, and one log of oil. The priest who pronounces them clean shall present both the one to be cleansed and their offerings before the LORD at the entrance to the tent of meeting." - Lev 14:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Three lambs, fine flour, oil. For someone who had spent months or years outside the camp, unable to work or farm or trade, this was an enormous cost. Where would they even get it?

That question matters, and God answers it further down the chapter — there is a reduced offering for those who cannot afford this. We will come to that. But notice first what the full offering represents: coming back to God is not casual, and it is not cheap.

We live in a time that can speak about grace carelessly, as if forgiveness were simply God overlooking things. Leviticus will not let us think that. Every step towards God's presence in this chapter walks past an altar. Something dies. Blood is shed. Without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness (Heb 9:22).

Grace is free to us. It was never free.

Look at what stands at the entrance to the tent of meeting: a person who could not cleanse themselves, and offerings they did not deserve. That is you and me. And the true cost was met not by three lambs but by one — you were redeemed... with the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or defect (1 Pet 1:18-19).

Hold your salvation with wonder today. It cost God everything.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you begun to treat forgiveness as something cheap?
2. What does it stir in you to consider what your cleansing cost?
3. How should the price of grace shape the way you live today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for ever treating Your grace lightly. Thank You that what I could never afford, Christ paid in full with His own blood. Amen.
